whyItWon: Semantic sharding plus per-file diagnostics converted an opaque red suite into two precise test regressions without changing runtime behavior. DIG Node QA #141 showed orchestration-authenticated-recovery.test.mjs failing from a misspelled crash variable and qubes-qrexec-campaign-harness.test.mjs failing because its expected object predated the collector provenance field. Fixing only those tests preserves the stronger lease-fencing and provenance contracts while minimizing regression risk and production cost.
failuresAndLessons: DIG Node QA #141 passed syntax-check, queue-core, worker-reliability, synthetic-sandboxes, orchestration benchmark, process fault, qrexec service, readiness gate, and campaign collector; failures were limited to authenticated-recovery and campaign-harness tests.
orchestration-authenticated-recovery.test.mjs used crashAfterRequestId as an undefined shorthand instead of mapping crashAfterRequestId: crashRequestId; the test failed before exercising the runtime.
qubes-qrexec-campaign-harness.test.mjs expected the pre-provenance collector shape; collectQrexecCampaign now deliberately returns provenance:null for unframed synthetic unit events.
When a security/reliability feature strengthens a returned contract, dependent tests must be updated explicitly rather than deleting or hiding the new field.
Production semantics should not be modified to repair fixture-only regressions when logs prove the runtime paths are otherwise passing.
Per-file diagnostics are worth retaining because they provide precise failure evidence with bounded runner use.
nextGate: require syntax-check, queue-core, worker-reliability, distributed-faults, and synthetic-sandboxes all green on the repaired head; then extend the Qubes campaign with same-workerId stale lease-token reclaim evidence before any real Qubes worker readiness decision
